reasons: Projects placed by country name look identical to projects with exact positions.
The legend lists four statuses but the colours cover seven.

terms.meaning: A drawing format built from shapes that stays sharp at any size in a browser.
Positions on Earth, north or south and east or west.
A common way of drawing the round Earth on a flat map.
The data for one project's dot on the map.
A group of nearby dots drawn as one marker.
A small box that appears when the cursor rests on something.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the React tools, the app's standard colours and the country location lookup.
sections.why: Standard setup. Shared colours keep the map matching the rest of the app.

sections.name: ProjectPin
sections.title: Shape of one map pin
sections.what: Describes one project as shown on the map: its name, country, power, status, position and whether its position is exact.
sections.why: Gives the map a fixed shape for its own calculations.

sections.name: ProjectMapProps
sections.title: Inputs the map accepts
sections.what: Describes what a parent page must pass in: the list of projects and two optional actions, one for clicking a single project and one for clicking a grouped marker to see its sources.
sections.why: Lets the same map be reused in several pages with different actions.
sections.watch_out: If the parent does not pass the sources action, clicking a grouped marker does nothing.

sections.name: mercatorX
sections.title: Horizontal position calculation
sections.what: Turns a longitude into a horizontal position on the 960 by 500 map canvas.
sections.why: Needed to draw dots on a flat picture of the world.

sections.name: mercatorY
sections.title: Vertical position calculation
sections.what: Turns a latitude into a vertical position using the Mercator method.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Mercator method is the standard style for a flat world map, and this matches the horizontal calculation.
sections.watch_out: The formula has no limit near the poles, so an extreme latitude would break the drawing.

sections.name: STATUS_COLORS
sections.title: Colours for each status
sections.what: Maps each project status to a colour: on track and completed to green, planned to blue, delayed and critical or over-budget to red, and paused to amber.
sections.why: Likely reason: so status can be read at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A status not in this list falls back to grey, and the legend does not explain grey.

sections.name: ProjectMap (part 1)
sections.title: Pin preparation and map state
sections.what: Builds the list of pins from the projects, skipping any without a known position and noting whether each position is exact. Also sets up the hover state for the tooltip.
sections.why: Likely reason: drawing is simpler once every project has a clean position.
sections.watch_out: Projects placed only by country are put at the country's middle point, so they look as precise as exact positions.

sections.name: ProjectMap: for
sections.title: Clustering and hover handling
sections.what: Groups pins that fall in the same 15-pixel square into one marker at their average position, adds up the power and picks the most common status. It also handles mouse-over and mouse-out for the tooltip.
sections.why: Likely reason: so crowded projects do not overlap into an unreadable blob.
sections.watch_out: The grouping uses a fixed size, so changing the canvas size in the code changes which projects group together.

sections.name: ProjectMap (part 3)
sections.title: Counts, legend and map lines
sections.what: Shows counts of mapped and unmapped projects, a small colour key, an SVG canvas with a faint grid, and two dashed lines for the equator and the prime meridian.
sections.why: Gives context on how complete the map is.
sections.watch_out: The colour key shows only four statuses, so the other colours are unexplained.

sections.name: ProjectMap (part 4)
sections.title: Drawing the markers
sections.what: Draws each group as two circles, a soft halo and a solid dot, sized by count and coloured by status. Groups of more than one show a number. Clicking a single project opens it, and clicking a group opens its sources list.
sections.why: Likely reason: the halo makes the marker under the cursor easy to see.
sections.watch_out: Marker size stops growing at a fixed maximum, so very large groups look the same size as moderately large ones.

sections.name: ProjectMap (part 5)
sections.title: Hover tooltip
sections.what: Shows a small box near the hovered marker with the country, the number of projects, up to five project names with their power and status colour, and a count of any remaining projects.
sections.why: Lets a reader see details without leaving the map.
sections.watch_out: The country shown is taken from the first project in the group, so a mixed group shows only one country.

sections.name: getMajorityStatus
sections.title: Most common status
sections.what: Picks the status that most projects in a group share. If two statuses tie, the one seen first wins.
sections.why: Gives each grouped marker a single colour.
sections.watch_out: Ties are settled by the order of the data, so the colour can change if the project list is reordered.

summary: An interactive world map that places each project as a coloured dot, groups nearby dots, and shows details on hover or click.
purpose: Lets the owner see where projects are, how they are doing, and move to a project from the map.
why: Likely reason: a picture of projects by location makes clusters easy to spot. A fuller reason is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Turn each project into a pin, skipping projects with no location. 2. Convert each pin's longitude and latitude into a flat map position. 3. Group pins that fall in the same small square. 4. Draw each group as a coloured dot with a count. 5. Show a tooltip on hover. 6. On click, open a single project or the list of sources for a group.
inputs: A list of projects with id, name, country, latitude, longitude, megawatts and status. Optional click actions from the parent. Country positions come from the country lookup when exact positions are missing.
outputs: A drawn map on screen and calls to the click actions. Nothing is saved.
risks: Country-level positions look the same as exact ones. Extreme latitudes would break the drawing. A group's colour can change with data order. Unknown statuses appear grey.
debug: If a project is missing, it probably has no usable location. The MAPPED and UNMAPPED counts show how many are missing. If a dot is in the wrong place, check its latitude and longitude. If clicks do nothing, check that the parent passes the click actions.
